newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bavarian bank merger boosts German bank shares.
newsitem.headline: Bavarian bank merger boosts German bank shares.

text.p: News that Bavarian banks Bayerische Hypo-Bank and Bayerische Vereinsbank were to merge excited equity traders in Frankfurt on Monday and put bank stocks firmly into focus in share trade.
In late trade on the IBIS DAX index, Vereinsbank was up 5.02 marks, or 6.12 percent, at 87 marks, while Hypo-Bank was up nine marks, or 15.52 percent, at 67 marks.
Both shares were off earlier all-time highs of 94.70 marks and 74 marks respectively, reached earlier in the day.

But dealers said that despite a series of interruptions to trade early on Monday because of technical problems, shares in the two banks held their own by the afternoon against pressure to take profits.
The IBIS DAX index of German shares rose around 1.7 percent at the open on the back of a positive reception to the news, which distracted from a huge drop on Wall Street on Friday.
"The markets were euphoric because of the banks and this pushed Wall Street weakness aside," a Frankfurt trader said.
By the afternoon some of the euphoria had worn off and the IBIS DAX index was down over 0.61 percent at 4,106.09 points, down 25.85.
Dealers said that without the banking sector supporting the market, the correction could have been more significant.
"If it were not for the banks, we would have been lower from the outset," said one dealer.
The news also brought focus to bear on other banking stocks. Dresdner Bank was up 3.40 marks at 78.66 marks and Commerzbank was up 2.96 marks at 56.46 marks.
Deutsche Bank rose 3.35 marks to 110.25 marks in early trade, then fell later on profit taking, before recovering in late trade to stand at 108.25 marks, up 1.35.
"This situation offers long-term upside potential for the whole sector, and we therefore reiterate our recommendation to overweight German banks," Trinkaus & Burhardt said in a research note.
"An expensive path of consolidation still lies ahead for the merging parties, which will create a good deal of room for disappointment after the initial euphoria subsides," it said.
Shares in insurer Allianz AG were down 18.10 marks, or 4.12 percent, at 420.90 marks in late IBIS trade.
Earlier Vereinsbank said it would offer Allianz shares to Hypo-Bank shareholders, with shareholders receiving one Allianz share for six Hypo-Bank shares.
The opening price for the Hypo-Bank share was close to the offer price, which equated to 75 marks per Hypo-Bank share on the basis of Friday's closing share prices.
Allianz AG said the share offer made as part of a bank merger would take up nine percent of its capital and said the merger would place up to nine billion marks of its shares.
In a compulsory statement, Allianz said it holds 22.1 percent of Hypo-Bank and four percent of Vereinsbank and will hold 15 percent of the merged bank, making it the largest shareholder.
The Allianz board had said it could not rule out that the merger and the share exchange would have an effect on the Allianz share price.
But Allianz said also the merger will increase the value of Allianz's stakes in Bavarian banks, also increasing its shareholder numbers and thereby its liquidity.
Allianz said the bank merger was optimal for the sale of insurance and asset plans. The share exchange would increase its holdings among small shareholders by between 20 percent and 25 percent.
